methods.analysis_type: Descriptive measured acoustics; no brain or clinical measurements
methods.feature_normalization: Power-weighted; full unpooled mean PSD, not the logarithmic display bins
limits: Per-recording relative spectrum and spectrogram normalization
Digital levels are not calibrated dB SPL
Personal comfort requires individual feedback; no sweet spot can be inferred from these recordings alone

spectrum.normalization: 0 dB is the maximum single-channel bin in this excerpt's mean one-sided power spectral density from 20 Hz to 8 kHz; both channels share that reference.
spectrum.high_frequency_pooling: Above 650 Hz, each logarithmic display bin retains the maximum power separately for each channel. These pooled points are for display, not feature calculations.

spectrogram.normalization: 0 dB is this excerpt's highest displayed time-frequency power, after averaging L/R power; colors cannot compare absolute levels between recordings.
spectrogram.method: 150 evenly spaced 4096-sample Hann windows; 96 logarithmic display bins. Narrow display bins interpolate the sampled PSD. This view cannot resolve sub-Hz carrier differences; use the long-window spectrum zooms.

envelope.method: Non-overlapping 100 ms RMS windows, 20 log10(RMS), with digital full-scale amplitude 1. This is a level envelope, not a modulation spectrum or calibrated listening volume.

features.method: Features use the unpooled mean one-sided power spectrum from 20 Hz to Nyquist. Flatness and centroid are power-based; spectral peaks are not automatically musical fundamentals.

tone_pairs.normalization: Both channels and both zoom panels share the largest bin in the full-excerpt, 30-second Hann-window spectrum as 0 dB.
tone_pairs.interpretation: These ear-separated stable carrier pairs are compatible with a binaural-stimulation design. They do not establish brain entrainment, pain relief, or a therapeutic frequency.
